We’ve all been there: staring at a cursor, thinking you need to sound like a 19th-century philosopher to get a First. Spoiler: your professor hates it as much as you do.

Slide 1: Stop trying to sound smart. Start trying to be clear.
Slide 2: The Myth. Using long, complex words to mask a lack of argument. It’s painful to read and usually hides a weak point.
Slide 3: The Reality. The best essays are the ones that explain complex ideas simply. Evidence + Logic > Jargon.
Slide 4: Your goal isn't to impress with a thesaurus; it’s to guide your reader through your argument without them needing a dictionary.

If you’re currently stuck in a jargon-filled hole, let’s get it sorted. Save this for when you’re editing your next draft and feeling the urge to 'fancy up' your sentences.

copy.facebook:
I was looking through some feedback on a student’s draft yesterday, and it hit me: so many of you are sabotaging your own grades by over-complicating your writing. 

We’ve all been taught that 'academic' means using big, clunky words. The truth? Your professor just wants to see that you understand the concepts. If you can’t explain it clearly, you probably haven’t grasped it yet. 

Here’s the reality check for your next submission:
• Stop using 'polysyllabic terminology' to sound scholarly.
• Focus on precision and evidence-based arguments.
• If your sentence is longer than three lines, cut it in half.

Clarity is the secret to high marks. If you’re feeling unsure about your current draft, don’t stress and let it sit there. Send me a message on WhatsApp at +91 95098 93638 and let’s look at it together. Let's make your writing work for you, not against you.
